Here is the same point again, in steps.

1. A capture joins a settlement batch. The cutoff is the last time a capture can join today's batch.
2. The payment service provider (PSP) moved the cutoff to 17:00 UTC.
3. A capture after 17:00 UTC on Friday joins Monday's settlement batch.
4. T+2 means the money arrives two business days after the batch closes. Monday plus two business days is Wednesday.
5. Reconciliation marks these payments as late until the ledger records them.
The cutoff moved. Late captures join the next batch.

fail.answer: The payout run slipped because the PSP moved the cutoff, so anything captured after 17:00 UTC rolls into the next batch and lands T+2 from that close rather than from today's, which is why Friday's captures show up Wednesday instead of Tuesday, and reconciliation will flag them as late until the ledger catches up.

Because the provider moved the cutoff earlier in the day the captures that happen after the new time on a Friday afternoon do not make it into that day's batch and instead wait for the Monday batch which then settles two business days later on Wednesday
